An extra bit makes the number of 1s even (even parity) or odd (odd parity); the receiver counts the 1s.

front: Weakness of a single parity bit
back: An even number of flipped bits is not detected, and it cannot show which bit is wrong.

front: How a parity block locates an error
back: The wrong bit is where the failing byte (row) and failing column (from the parity byte) cross.
A value calculated from a block of data, sent with it, recalculated by the receiver and compared.
The receiver sends the data back; the sender compares it with the original.
An extra digit calculated from the others in a number (ISBN, bar code) to detect data-entry errors.
Receiver sends positive/negative acknowledgements; a negative acknowledgement or a timeout makes the sender resend.
